_comment: The files players find (world/files/LabFiles). Each is a block rl_doc_<id> in the world; G reads it and the kit's Files page keeps it. Sets group them on the page. Bodies use \n for paragraphs.

files.title: Welcome to Ridgeview
files.body:
Welcome to Ridgeview Laboratories. Your badge opens the headhouse and B1. Access below B1 is by programme only.
Do not discuss your work outside the site, with family, or with staff from other floors. If you are asked what Ridgeview does, the answer is materials research.
The canteen on B1 is open 06:00 to 22:00. The lifts are out of service. Use the stairs.

files.title: Threshold: phase two approved
files.body:
Funding for phase two of Threshold is approved. The ring will be run at full field for the first time on 4 March.
I know some of you have doubts about the readings from the February tests. So do I. That is why we are going further, not stopping.
Whatever is on the other side of that field has been there a long time. We will be the first to see it. Keep the logs clean.

files.title: Ring test log, 4 March
files.body:
14:02 Field to 40%. Hum as expected.
14:09 Field to 80%. Air pressure in the hall dropping. Temperature at the ring up 30 degrees.
14:11 Full field. The centre of the ring is no longer dark. Cameras show a red light, then depth. It is not a reflection.
14:11 Air is moving INTO the hall. Ash on the floor. Smell of sulphur.
14:13 Field dropped. Opening closed. Nobody leaves the hall until decon.

files.title: Probe recovery
files.body:
Probe 3 came back after eleven minutes on the far side. Surface temperature 380 degrees. The casing is pitted like it sat in acid.
The air sample canister was full of a fine red dust. Under the scope it is not dust. It is spores. Thousands to the millilitre.
I've put the canister in the glove box on B2 and sealed the room. I don't want anyone opening it without a suit.

files.title: Specimen R, growth notes
files.body:
The spores ignore every culture medium we give them. They only germinate on dead tissue.
We gave them a dead lab mouse. In nine hours the body was threaded with red filaments. In twenty hours it moved.
Not twitching. It got up. It went for the glass when I leaned close.
I'm calling it Specimen R until someone above me gives it a name. I have stopped sleeping.

files.title: Memo: handling the red material
files.body:
With immediate effect, all work with Specimen R is BSL-4. Pressure suits only. Two people in the room at all times.
The material survives the decon shower. It survives bleach at normal strength. It does not survive fire.
Any scratch or bite from an exposed animal is to be reported at once. Do not wait to see if it gets better.

files.title: Something came through
files.body:
02:40 Unscheduled field rise. Nobody on the desk touched it. The ring powered itself from the plant.
02:41 Opening at full size. Something moved on the far side.
02:42 It came through. Tall. Too many legs. It stood in the hall and looked up at the gallery.
02:44 Field dropped when the breakers blew. It is still in the hall. It is not moving. Calling security.

files.title: Containment of the specimen
files.body:
The specimen was taken in the hall at 05:15 with sedative gas pumped through the vents. It took three times the dose we use for a horse.
Two of my men are in the infirmary. One of them is not expected to live. It did not bite him. It lifted him off the floor with the blades on its front and carried him toward the ring.
It is in the big tank on B2 now. The staff are calling it the Harvestman. I don't like that they've given it a name.

files.title: The Harvestman, first observations
files.body:
It is not asleep in the tank. Its eyes follow whoever stands nearest.
It carries no spores itself, but everything it touches does. I think it lives alongside them over there. They grow in what it kills, and it eats what they grow.
It watched Daniel for six hours yesterday. He has asked to be moved off this floor. I said yes.

files.title: Surge log
files.body:
8 Apr 03:14 Field rise, no input. 40 seconds. Red light in the hall.
11 Apr 22:50 Field rise. 2 minutes. Ash on the gallery.
12 Apr 04:02 Field rise. Hall cameras lost. Something on the floor when they came back. Gone by the time the team got down.
15 Apr 01:30 Field rise. Third this week. The ring isn't drawing from our plant any more. It's drawing from somewhere else.

files.title: Request to shut the ring down
files.body:
Director,
I am asking you again to shut the ring down for good and pour the hall.
It opens on its own now. Each time, something comes through or something of ours goes missing. The spores are in the B3 ducting. I found them growing in the drain of the decon line.
We are not studying that place any more. It is studying us.

files.title: Order to seal the ring hall
files.body:
Threshold is suspended. The ring hall is to be filled with concrete tonight, through the ring itself, in one pour.
All staff below B1 report to decon by 20:00. Anyone not through decon by 22:00 will be left below.
I want it understood that I was right to go on. We learned more in seven weeks than in seven years. We simply learned it too fast.

files.title: Torn page, no name
files.body:
the tank is cracked. it got out while the power was down. we heard it in the vents all night.
mark from B3 came up the stairs this morning and he wasnt right. red in his eyes. he bit gail.
the plug is cracked too. you can see the light through it at night.
whoever reads this dont go down to the hall

files.title: Last entry, ring control
files.body:
Plug cracked overnight. Heat through the cracks. Field reading on the ring with no power at all.
B2 has gone quiet. B3 lights are failing.
If the army is reading this: the ring is not the problem. The ring was a door. The problem is what is on the other side, and that it knows where the door is now.
Do not try to open it. Do not try to close it. Burn everything that comes out.

files.title: Order 1: cordon Ridgeview
files.body:
Ridgeview Laboratories and the ground for three kilometres round it are a quarantine zone from 06:00.
Roads into the Black Pine Mountains are closed at the ridge. No civilian enters or leaves.
Troops are to wear masks inside the wire. The red growth on the ground near the site is not to be touched, walked through or burned without orders.

files.title: Rules of engagement
files.body:
Anyone coming out of the zone who does not stop at the line is to be stopped.
The sick do not answer to their names. They do not feel pain. Aim for the head.
There is a second kind of threat inside the wire. It is tall, it climbs, and it takes men away. Do not go after anyone it takes.

files.title: Aid station log
files.body:
41 brought in today with bites or the red rash. 12 turned before nightfall.
The rash starts at the wound and spreads under the skin like roots. Fever. Then nothing. Then they get up.
We have stopped treating. We are only sorting now. Masks do help, but only if they never come off.

files.title: Burn pit detail
files.body:
Burn pit lit at 18:00. 60 bodies.
The ones that had been in the growth longest still moved in the fire. Keep the line back twenty metres and don't let anyone stand downwind.
The ash comes down over the whole camp now. Cover the water.

files.title: Order 6: fall back
files.body:
The Ridgeview cordon is broken on the north and east sides.
All units fall back to the ridge road and then to Fort Caldwell. Leave the vehicles that will not start. Leave the tents.
Cases have been reported in the county. The quarantine is no longer one site. It is everywhere.

files.title: Radio log, gate
files.body:
21:10 Gate to command, no answer.
21:20 Lights in the trees, red, low down. Not vehicles.
21:35 They're coming out of the growth. Dozens.
21:36 There's something tall behind them. It's on the tower. It's on the tower.
21:37 [no further entries]

files.title: Field notes: what it wants
files.body:
It does not eat the infected. It eats people who are still whole. It will drag a body a long way to somewhere dark and high, and it comes back to the same places.
It picks one person and follows them for days. It waits outside doors. It goes quiet when it is close.
If it has chosen you, stay in the light and never sleep alone.

files.title: Weak points
files.body:
Rifle rounds bounce off the plates on its back. The belly is soft, and so are the eyes, three on each side of the head.
It can lose a leg and keep coming. It goes back to its den and builds the leg again from scrap over a day or so.
It hates fire. It hates noise less than you would think.

files.title: Note pinned to a door
files.body:
We came down from Black Pine. The ground up there is red and soft and it moves when you aren't looking at it.
Don't drink from the streams that run off the mountain. Don't sleep near the red stuff.
If you hear a long scraping on the roof at night, turn your lights off and wait.

files.title: Diary page
files.body:
Day 12. The radio says it started in a lab in the mountains. Some kind of experiment. They say there's a door up there that should never have been opened.
Day 13. Someone on the radio says the door still opens sometimes, at night, and when it does more of them come out.
Day 14. No radio.
